results.fact: Total elevation gain (gain_ft vs loss_ft vs itinerary)
results.evidence: loss_ft, the itinerary day gains (3100+4200+300), and totalNote all agree on 7,600 ft; gain_ft 3500 is the only outlier (it roughly matches a single summit-day figure). Bird Creek Camp sits at 4,200 ft about 4 mi above Weaver Point (~1,100 ft), and the camp-to-summit climb is about 4,800 ft of gain, so car-to-car totals ~7,500-7,900 ft. Descent_text's '~4,000+ ft' loss back to Weaver Point also understates the ~7,200 ft drop from 8,383 ft.

results.correct_value: 17.7 km (~11 mi one way from the Harlequin Bridge stop)
results.evidence: dist_km 5.6 km (3.5 mi) is the camp-to-summit leg only (a 7 mi round trip from the Bird Creek bivy). The one-way approach is ~3.5 mi Harlequin Bridge to Weaver Point, ~4 mi up Devore Creek Trail to Bird Creek Camp, then ~3.5 mi to the summit — about 11 mi, which matches the route's own summit waypoint distMi 11 and the ~25 mi round-trip itinerary.

results.fact: Whether fixed rappel anchors exist on the crux/summit step
results.correct_value: Left-in-place (slung) rappel anchors exist at the edge of the summit ridge, above the 20-ft crux step, and at the summit block; no bolts or chains
results.evidence: One trip report found a rap anchor at the summit-ridge edge, another on top of the 20-ft crux, and a good rap anchor at the summit block, and rappelled from them. A second report describes a conveniently located rap station at the top of the 4th-class step and a second rap below. Descent_text's claim of no fixed hardware and building your own natural anchor is the outlier.

patches.fact: Whether fixed rappel anchors exist on the crux/summit step
patches.find: there are no fixed bolts, chains, or any other fixed hardware on this route, so if you choose to rappel it rather than downclimb, you'll build a natural anchor (webbing/cord around a horn or block) and retrieve your gear, or downclimb it with a spot/handline
patches.replace: there are no bolts or chains, but slung rappel anchors have been found left in place at the edge of the summit ridge, above the crux step and at the summit block — inspect any webbing and carry spare cord to back it up or build your own, or downclimb it with a spot/handline

results.fact: Bird Creek Camp's elevation and position
results.correct_value: Bird Creek Camp ~4,200 ft, about 4 mi up the Devore Creek Trail from Weaver Point
results.evidence: Bird Creek Campground is about 4 miles from Weaver Point on the Devore Creek Trail at 4,200 ft; a second report camps at the 4,200 ft Devore/Bird Creek junction. The waypoint's 5,800 ft, and the beta and pitch_detail[0] copies saying ~5,400 ft, are wrong (5,400 ft is the unofficial higher camp). Waypoint distMi left as is (distance counted from Harlequin Bridge).
